new_findings_today.title: CARTO's free/keyless raster basemap tiles now return an 'API KEY REQUIRED' placeholder image instead of real map tiles -- breaks the visual basemap on every Leaflet-template surface sitewide (external vendor issue, not a NakshIQ code regression)
new_findings_today.detail: While running Section K's routine /en/explore map-toggle check, the Leaflet map rendered with markers correctly plotted but no legible basemap underneath. Extracted the actual tile URL the live page requests (https://c.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_nolabels/{z}/{x}/{y}{r}.png, e.g. .../5/22/13.png) and fetched it directly: HTTP 200, valid PNG, but the decoded image has 'API KEY REQUIRED -- carto.com/basemaps/apikey' baked into it as a diagonal watermark over a near-black background. Reproduced identically on all 3 CARTO subdomains (a/b/c.basemaps.cartocdn.com). The sibling 'dark_only_labels' tile layer (place-name text only, used by the same components) still renders correctly -- fetched and viewed a sample tile showing real labels (Amritsar, PAKISTAN, NEW DELHI, Jaipur, Bhopal, Ahmedabad, INDIA) with no watermark, so only the base terrain/imagery layer is affected, not the labels overlay. Grepped for every component requesting this URL pattern: apps/web/src/components/explore-map.tsx, destination-map.tsx, and trek-trail-map.tsx all use the identical unauthenticated https://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_nolabels/{z}/{x}/{y}{r}.png + dark_only_labels pair. git log on all 3 files shows no relevant change (explore-map.tsx last touched 2026-07-16 for CSP/SRI hardening, unrelated to tile URLs) -- this is not a NakshIQ code regression, it reads as an external change on CARTO's side to their free/anonymous raster-tile policy (or a quota/rate condition manifesting as a hard block). Live-verified the user-visible effect on 2 of the 3 affected surfaces: /en/explore's Map view shows 519 markers correctly positioned but floating over an unreadable watermarked/blank background; /en/destination/betla's inline destination map (a live, in-sample, non-cinematic destination today) shows a fully blank dark rectangle with no legible geography at all. Leaflet mechanics are completely unaffected -- container mounts, tiles request successfully (just wrong content), markers render, window.L is present, and 0 console errors are thrown anywhere, because the tile requests technically succeed (HTTP 200) -- this is why no prior QA session's Section K methodology (which only ever counted .leaflet-container/.leaflet-tile/.leaflet-interactive elements, never inspected actual tile pixel content) caught this.
new_findings_today.evidence: Direct fetch of https://c.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_nolabels/5/22/13.png (and the a/b subdomain variants): all HTTP 200, image/png, 7907 bytes, decoded image shows the 'API KEY REQUIRED' watermark (viewed directly). Direct fetch of https://a.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_only_labels/5/22/13.png: HTTP 200, 4836 bytes, decoded image shows real, correct place-name labels with no watermark. grep -n 'cartocdn|basemap|tileLayer' across apps/web/src/components/{explore-map,destination-map,trek-trail-map}.tsx confirms all 3 use the identical URL template with no API key parameter. `git log -5` on all 3 files shows no commit remotely close to today or addressing tile auth. Chrome screenshots: /en/explore Map view (519 markers over broken tiles) and /en/destination/betla (fully blank map rectangle, zoomed screenshot confirms no legible content).
new_findings_today.recommendation: Register a CARTO account and add the required API key to the 3 tileLayer calls (or migrate to a different provider -- plain OpenStreetMap raster tiles, MapTiler's free tier, or Stadia Maps all have generous free keyless/low-key options for a site this size). This is a visible, sitewide degradation of a core interactive feature (the /explore map is top-nav-accessible) and should be prioritized above the other, lower-visibility findings in this report. Also worth adding a tile-content spot-check (not just tile-count) to Section K's standing methodology going forward, since this class of failure is invisible to every check this harness has run until today.
